items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1972-04-05
items.q: I fixed it so that, uh, with Joe Wolf, I could lay off and come back after the dance

ctx.x: I'll tell you how it happened. I was hustling. That time I was a gambler. A lot of ways, that's all I, I didn't do no work or nothing. I'd just catch it what I could. And, uh, running around from district to district. What happened, this colored fellow that worked for the Whitney, he was in a barber shop. Smallwood's barber shop on a rampart near, near, near Gravia. Uh, and, uh, happened, this thing come up by the work fight or go to jail. Well, I was dodging the police, you see, cause I didn't have no job or…

Wolf over there, he was in charge of all the, all the, the building help. And I, I, I said, well now, uh, when, when René had to get a job for that night, I couldn't, I had to work, and I couldn't get off, so I fixed it so that, uh, with Joe Wolf, I could lay off and come back after the dance and stay till in the morning, you know, till daylight in the morning, catch up my job, you know, catch up my work. And he told me that it would be alright. So if I had a job till twelve o'clock at night, I could come back,…
